candidates.title: Binary black-hole mergers with ultralight vector bosons
candidates.abstract: We simulate the inspiral, merger, and ringdown of equal-mass, nonspinning binary black holes coupled to a massive vector (Proca) field. Starting from constraint-consistent electric-field initial data, we find that the Proca field rapidly concentrates around the black holes. However, it continues to exhibit nontrivial dynamics. Orbital evolution depends on vector mass, while the dominant gravitational waveforms remain close to vacuum after time, phase, and amplitude alignment. This contrast highlights the limited imprint of the field on aligned merger-ringdown morphology at these resolutions.

candidates.title: Detectability of Eccentric Intermediate Mass-Ratio Inspiral in the Decihertz Band
candidates.abstract: The proposed decihertz gravitational-wave (GW) band $(\sim 10^{-2}-1\,\Hz)$ will observe the late inspiral of intermediate mass-ratio inspirals (IMRIs), binaries with mass ratios $10^2 \lesssim q \lesssim 10^4$ that assemble dynamically in dense stellar environments and are expected to retain measurable eccentricity. Search and parameter-estimation pipelines are predominantly built around circular templates, and we test this assumption. Using black-hole perturbation theory waveforms from \textsc{FastEMRIWaveforms} for a representative IMRI ($M=10^4\,\modot$, $q=100$, observed for its final $10\,\hr$), we compute fitting factors between eccentric signals and circular templates, maximizing over the template's total mass and mass ratio with a differential-evolution search, for the B-DECIGO, LGWA-Si, and IndIGO-D noise curves and a flat PSD. The mismatch grows with initial eccentricity $e_0$ and crosses the standard $3\%$ threshold at $e_0\simeq3\times10^{-2}$, well within the range allowed by the waveform model and expected from dynamical formation. The best-fitting circular templates also bias the total mass and mass ratio by several percent at $e_0=0.1$. Combining the mismatch with the signal-to-noise-dependent distinguishability criterion, we find that for a source at $1\,\mathrm{Gpc}$, eccentricities as small as $e_0\simeq5\times10^{-4}$ (B-DECIGO and IndIGO-D) and $5\times10^{-3}$ (LGWA-Si) are resolvable, one to two orders of magnitude below where detection efficiency degrades. The loss of match arises from the excitation of radial Teukolsky harmonics, which spread power into sidebands that circular templates cannot represent, and from the slower orbital decay of eccentric binaries at fixed initial semi-latus rectum. Robust detection and parameter estimation of IMRIs with DECIGO, LGWA, and IndIGO-D will require eccentric waveform models and template banks.

candidates.title: Gravitational waves from cosmological first-order phase transitions with fluctuation-induced friction
candidates.abstract: We study gravitational-wave production in a cosmological first-order phase transition with fluctuation-induced friction using three-dimensional lattice simulations of two coupled scalar fields. Kinetic and gradient energy in the additional field $s$ accumulates near the expanding bubble walls of $φ$ and affects their motion. The contribution from $s$ exceeds that from $φ$ at the spectral peak and has a slope similar to that of the bulk flow model over a finite interval above the peak. In the high-wave-number (UV) direction, $φ$ dominates and the total spectrum develops a broad feature. For the larger coupling, slowly contracting false vacuum remnants persist long after bubble merger.

candidates.title: Gravitational Mode Instabilities in Kerr-like Black Holes
candidates.abstract: We identify exponentially growing modes of a homogeneous gravitational Teukolsky-like operator on highly spinning Kerr-like black holes subject to quasinormal mode boundary conditions. Specifically, we compute electromagnetic and gravitational quasinormal modes of a spacetime proposed by Konoplya, Rezzolla, and Zhidenko that parametrizes deformations from the Kerr geometry, including configurations with black hole spin parameter $a/M > 1$ that retain an event horizon. Using the continued fraction method, we find that the spin-weight $s=-2$ operator develops exponentially growing modes when the black hole spin and deformation parameters are sufficiently large, while the electromagnetic modes remain damped throughout the parameter space. We further compare the quasinormal mode predictions with an agnostic analysis of the GW250114 ringdown, identifying regions of the parameter space that are compatible with the spectrum inferred from the data.

candidates.title: Pulsar timing response and observational constraints on continuous-spin gravity
candidates.abstract: Continuous-spin particles form the most general massless integer-helicity irreducible representations of the Poincaré group, characterized by a dimensionful continuous-spin scale $ρ_g$ set by a nonzero Pauli--Lubanski invariant. A single continuous-spin representation contains an infinite tower of integer helicities $h\in\mathbb Z$ that mix under Lorentz boosts. Since continuous-spin effects are controlled by $α\equivρ_g/(\hbarω)$ at gravitational-wave angular frequency $ω$, nanohertz pulsar timing arrays are naturally sensitive to ultralow values of $ρ_g$. Starting from the gauge-invariant worldline coupling of linearized continuous-spin gravity, we derive the one-way pulsar timing redshift response and the overlap reduction function of an isotropic stochastic background for arbitrary integer helicity. We show that while photon propagation is modulated across all helicities, only the vector modes ($h=\pm1$) perturb the four-velocity of a static observer, and that the tensor modes ($h=\pm2$) smoothly recover the Hellings--Downs correlation of general relativity as $ρ_g/(\hbarω)\to 0$. Modeling an unpolarized $h=\pm2$ background in the solar-system barycentric frame and jointly fitting the NANOGrav 15-year data with pulsar red noise, we obtain the $95\%$ upper limits $ρ^{U}_g<7.03\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}$ and $ρ^{\log {U}}_g<4.79\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}$ under uniform and log-uniform priors, respectively. Under the uniform prior, we obtain $γ_{\mathrm{GW}} = 4.89^{+0.85}_{-0.96}$, which brings the spectral index closer to the canonical value $γ_{\rm GW}=13/3$ expected for circular SMBHBs than standard General Relativity.

candidates.title: Fundamental physics with quantum sensors in space
candidates.abstract: Quantum sensors such as atomic clocks, atom interferometers, and atomic magnetometers can be used as sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model. Space offers microgravity, long baselines, low environmental noise, access to varying gravitational potentials, and unique opportunities involving the Sun, Moon, planets, and asteroids. These proceedings of the Aspen Center for Physics workshop on "Fundamental physics in space with quantum sensors," held February 22-27, 2026, summarize the scientific case, current capabilities, and space mission concepts for investigating dark matter, testing general relativity, and detecting gravitational waves in frequency bands inaccessible from the ground.

analysis.zh_summary: Quantum sensors such as atomic clocks, atom interferometers, and atomic magnetometers can be used as sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model.

candidates.title: Finite-wavelength corrections to dynamical friction in fuzzy dark matter: a causal linear-response approach
candidates.abstract: A massive body moving through fuzzy dark matter (FDM) generates a density wake whose gravitational backreaction produces dynamical friction. We investigate how finite-wavelength effects modify this force using causal linear-response theory and the statistical Wigner formulation. For a homogeneous Maxwellian background and general isotropic finite-size perturbers, we derive an analytic representation of the gravitational drag and recover the classical Chandrasekhar result under matched regularization conditions. In the controlled semiclassical regime, the leading finite-wavelength correction is quadratic in $\hbar/m_χ$ and factorizes into a velocity-dependent function and a ratio of spectral moments characterizing the source structure. Remarkably, this correction reduces the drag magnitude independently of the detailed radial source profile within the adopted Maxwellian model. Gaussian and exponential sources illustrate this result. We further establish a controlled remainder bound and clarify the nonuniform behavior of the point-source limit. These findings identify the physical conditions under which wave effects modify classical dynamical friction.

candidates.title: Self-gravitating Lee-Huang-Yang fluids as dark matter halos
candidates.abstract: We propose a model of dark matter halos based on a self-gravitating Bose fluid whose effective equation of state is dominated by Lee-Huang-Yang quantum fluctuations. The model is governed by coupled generalized Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson equations, which incorporate quantum pressure, Lee-Huang-Yang-induced repulsion, and gravitational attraction. By retaining the full quantum pressure, we examine the halo structure from its central region to its asymptotic regime. We first derive the Jeans dispersion relation and analyze how the Lee-Huang-Yang fluctuations alter the gravitational instability criterion and the associated characteristic length and mass scales. We then obtain analytical expressions for the central and large-radius behaviors of the equilibrium solutions. To verify the validity and the performance of the model, we fit the model-predicted curves with a sample of 20 galaxies from the SPARC database and compare the results with those obtained from Navarro-Frenk-White, standard Bose-Einstein condensate, and quantum-droplet dark matter models. We find that the pure-LHY model reproduces a broad range of observed galactic kinematics, yielding reduced $χ^2$ values and a lower sample average compared to the aforementioned models. These results indicate that the combined effects of quantum pressure, LHY quantum fluctuations and the self-gravity provide additional flexibility in describing both the central and extended outer regions of galactic halos. We also discuss the implications of the inferred halo parameters and emphasize their dependence on the assumed effective equation of state and its microscopic interpretation. The pure-LHY model constitutes an ideal platform for exploring the role of quantum-fluctuation-induced interaction in the formation and structure of dark matter halos.

candidates.title: Geometric optics for gravitational waves in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity: amplitude birefringence and tensor-scalar mixing on general backgrounds
candidates.abstract: We study the propagation of high-frequency gravitational waves in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity within the geometric optics approximation. In contrast to previous work, we allow for a general background with a nonvanishing scalar field, which enables a covariant treatment of amplitude birefringence. The background scalar gradient introduces third-derivative terms into the linearized field equations. These must be treated as subleading for the linearized system to be free of ghosts, which yields a covariant upper bound on the frequency. Tensor-scalar mixing is induced by the Weyl curvature through the Newman-Penrose scalar $Ψ_0$ along the ray. When the mixing is efficient, the propagation eigenmodes consist of one luminal, one subluminal, and one superluminal mode, and a violation of the ghost-free condition leads to a classical instability. From the transport equations at next-to-leading order, we show that, when the mixing is negligible, the relative amplitude of the two helicities depends only on the scalar-field gradients along the ray at the emission and observation events, independently of the path in between.

analysis.zh_summary: We study the propagation of high-frequency gravitational waves in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity within the geometric optics approximation.

candidates.title: Relativistic tidal excitation of g- and i-modes in neutron star binaries
candidates.abstract: When the gravitational wave frequency of an inspiraling binary matches a normal-mode frequency of a neutron star (NS), the mode can be resonantly excited. The excitation transfers orbital energy to the star and shifts the phase of the emitted gravitational-wave (GW) signal, thereby providing a potential probe of the NS interior. However, estimates of this phase shift in the literature vary by orders of magnitude due to different approximations and formulations used in calculating the tidal coupling strength. We revisit this problem using a fully relativistic scattering formalism, which serves as our benchmark calculation and provides a gauge-invariant mode response together with an effective tidal-mode coupling strength. We calculate the phase shifts induced by the excitation of stratification g-modes, crustal interface i-modes, and hadron-quark interface i-modes, and estimate their detectability with Fisher-matrix forecasts for current and next-generation detectors. In our models, direct g-mode excitation remains below the detection thresholds, even for the strongest stratification considered. Crust-core i-modes at large shear speeds provide the most favorable prospects and crust melting can produce a substantially larger phase shift. Hadron-quark i-modes remain below the next-generation detection thresholds.

candidates.title: Critical curves and throat degeneracy in black bounces
candidates.abstract: Identical critical curves need not imply identical null-orbit dynamics. For a class of static spherical areal-radius deformations, we show that a surviving original photon sphere retains its critical impact parameter and orbital frequency, while its coordinate-time Lyapunov exponent is multiplied by the radial Jacobian. The logarithmic strong-deflection coefficient acquires the inverse factor. At a reflection-symmetric throat, stability factorizes into a derivative of the original optical potential and the throat curvature. More generally, an order-$m$ extremum of the original potential composed with an order-$q$ areal-radius minimum produces an optical degeneracy of order $p=mq$, with critical approach $|x|\propto|t|^{-2/(p-2)}$ and reflected strong deflection $Δφ\propto(b/b_{\rm c}-1)^{-(p-2)/(2p)}$ for $p>2$. For the Simpson--Visser family with mass $M$ and bounce parameter $a$, the critical impact parameter remains Schwarzschild-like for $a<3M$, although the instability varies with $a$. The merger at $a=3M$ is quartic, separating stable and unstable throat branches. These results isolate the null-orbit information preserved by a radial deformation from that encoded in its local geometry.

candidates.title: Using the 0i Einstein equation to break dark-sector degeneracies
candidates.abstract: Over the past decade, cosmological observations have started to challenge the $Λ$CDM model. If these tensions persist, they immediately raise one fundamental question: what new physics could be responsible for them? More specifically, do these deviations arise from a modification of gravity, from an evolving or clustering dark energy component, or from dark matter properties beyond the cold dark matter paradigm? In this paper we show that, with current methods, any observed deviation can always be attributed to more than one sector, preventing us from determining if the tension is due to gravity, dark energy or dark matter. The main reason is that current tests rely on unobservable quantities. These quantities are then either related to observables by assuming the validity of specific equations, or compared with theoretical predictions computed within a given class of theories. Both approaches inevitably break the model independence of the tests, leading to degeneracies between gravity, dark energy, and dark matter. To overcome this limitation, we construct a set of three tests that rely only on observable quantities and that, when combined, can distinguish between the three sectors. We show that the $0i$ Einstein equation -- which is never tested in standard analyses -- adds crucial information to that provided by the gravitational slip equation and the Euler equation.

candidates.title: Cosmic Censorship in the Landscape of SUSY-Broken AdS Vacua
candidates.abstract: We investigate signatures of weak cosmic censorship in non-supersymmetric vacua of both IIA and IIB string theory. In particular, we examine the Penrose Inequality, which can be proven holographically using Ryu-Takayanagi, and can be independently proven in SUSY AdS vacua for spherically symmetric initial data. We prove that any EFT of scalars coupled to gravity in AdS, including in particular those of string compactifications, satisfies both the Penrose Inequality and a positive mass theorem if a function that we call a "weak fake superpotential" exists. We demonstrate that this condition is satisfied globally for the DGKT skew-whiffed vacua in IIA. Since there is no known nonperturbative instability in this DGKT vacuum, this provides evidence that the IIA SUSY-broken AdS vacua may be absolutely stable. We also find the weak fake superpotential exists locally in field space in some SUSY-broken AdS vacua in a KKLT construction in IIB. Thus, within the framework considered here, some false SUSY-broken KKLT AdS vacua are stable against vacuum decay. Conversely, we find that some KKLT vacua do not have a weak fake superpotential, and correspondingly violate the Penrose Inequality and fail to have a positive mass theorem; the DGKT vacua only violate the Penrose Inequality in the presence of designer gravity boundary conditions. In all cases studied, this is due to false vacuum decay. We discuss the implications of these violations for holography and black hole thermodynamics in these SUSY-broken AdS vacua.

analysis.zh_summary: We investigate signatures of weak cosmic censorship in non-supersymmetric vacua of both IIA and IIB string theory.

candidates.title: Separation of gravitational perturbations of Myers-Perry black holes
candidates.abstract: We study linearized gravitational perturbations of five-dimensional asymptotically flat Myers--Perry black holes with two unequal spins. We construct separated solutions for the five coupled gauge-invariant polarizations for arbitrary azimuthal mode numbers. The key observation is that the Killing--Yano symmetry induces a first-order angular operator that, together with a commuting second-order operator, determines the angular profiles of all five gravitational polarizations. The Carter interchange relates the scalar angular and radial equations, and the five tidal components of each separated solution share a single radial amplitude. We prove completeness of the angular harmonics at real frequencies and show that the resulting physical perturbations admit local metric reconstruction. In the singly spinning limit, we recover Santos's angular operators and radial equation for perturbations with $m_ψ=0$ and even parity under $ψ\to-ψ$. These results provide a framework for studying quasinormal modes and gravitational stability of five-dimensional rotating black holes with two independent spins.

candidates.title: Beyond the point lens: radial structure and the horizon in wave-optics gravitational lensing
candidates.abstract: Gravitational-wave lensing in the wave-optics regime is sensitive to the structure of the lens beyond its total mass: to its exterior radial profile and, as we show, to the boundary condition at its centre. We develop an analytic framework to compute these effects for a scalar wave, as corrections to the wave lensed by a Newtonian point mass. The corrections are organized in inverse powers of the distance from the lens and computed with dressed radial kernels, which include the Newtonian interaction to all orders and resum the long-range phase that invalidates the Born expansion around the free wave. Retaining wavefront curvature, we find that the scattered wave is not the whole response: an inverse-square deformation changes the direct wave by an equal amount, even when the scattered wave is faint. Steeper terms of the exterior potential lead to short-distance divergences, which signal that the exterior geometry alone does not determine the lensed wave: the missing information is a set of local terms fixed by the inner boundary condition. For a Schwarzschild black hole we determine them by matching to the ingoing solution at the horizon. The horizon enters the amplification factor as an absorptive contact term, which reproduces the horizon-area cross section; it is absent for a non-absorbing lens of the same mass, and cannot be described by the thin-lens diffraction integral. It completes the correction quadratic in the mass, where it appears at the same order as finite-distance optical corrections, and largely cancels against them for an aligned source. Together, these results connect Newtonian dressing, diffraction and inner boundary conditions, in a systematic description of corrections to point-mass gravitational-wave lensing.

analysis.zh_summary: Gravitational-wave lensing in the wave-optics regime is sensitive to the structure of the lens beyond its total mass: to its exterior radial profile and, as we show, to the boundary condition at its centre.

candidates.title: Regular/Singular Black Hole Thermodynamics from Renormalised Volume/Area
candidates.abstract: We study the finite mismatch between the holographically and topologically renormalised Euclidean actions of the four-dimensional AdS C-metric. Starting from the relation between Renormalised Volume and the Einstein sector of Conformal Gravity, we separate the regular curvature contribution from the contributions supported on the two conical axes. After introducing the usual Euler normalisation for smooth manifolds, the residual difference between the regular action evaluations is determined by the tension-weighted Euler terms of the renormalised worldsheet area. We identify this difference with the Gauss--Bonnet entropy contribution at the polar conical points of the horizon. The ordinary Euler characteristic remains fixed, while the deficits determine how its curvature representation is divided between regular and singular contributions. At fixed total string tension, the difference of the renormalised worldsheet areas per unit Euclidean time determines the relative tension work, giving a geometric interpretation of the relative thermodynamic length.

candidates.title: Supersymmetric warped AdS$_3$ solutions in eleven-dimensional supergravity
candidates.abstract: We construct new families of supersymmetric solutions of eleven-dimensional supergravity by deforming the half-BPS $\mathrm{AdS}_3\times \mathrm{S}^3_+\times \mathrm{S}^3_-\times\mathbb R^2$ background. We consider lightlike, spacelike and timelike warpings of the anti-de Sitter factor, accompanied by deformations of the two three-spheres, and determine the supporting four-form fluxes and the constraints imposed by the equations of motion. In particular, the deformation parameters of the two spheres are necessarily equal, although their radii need not coincide. We compute the conserved charges and determine the preserved supersymmetries and Killing superalgebras. Generic lightlike solutions preserve four real supercharges, whereas spacelike and timelike solutions preserve eight, with a Killing superalgebra containing a single exceptional $\mathfrak d(2,1;α)$ factor.

candidates.title: Geometry of squeezed states. The phase-space metric, relative vacua and cosmology
candidates.abstract: Geometry enters quantum theory in two places. The space of quantum states carries a symplectic form, which generates unitary evolution, and a metric, which governs uncertainties and transition probabilities. The classical phase space acquires a metric of its own when a vacuum is chosen: quantizing a linear system amounts to choosing a compatible complex structure, equivalently a compatible metric $g$. We take this second metric as the primary object and show that it plays, on phase space, the role that the quantum metric plays on the space of states: fluctuations of linear observables are $g$-norms of Hamiltonian vector fields, and along coherent states $g/2\hbar$ \emph{is} the quantum metric. Squeezed states then have a simple description. A squeezed vacuum is the vacuum of another metric, and squeezing is a property of a pair of metrics, a relative vacuum, whose invariants are the eigenvalues $e^{\pm2r_i}$ of $L=g_0^{-1}g$. We work out the harmonic oscillator in detail, including why a rotated squeezed state no longer minimizes the product of the displayed uncertainties. Quadratic evolution deforms the metric, and only the part of the generator that is self-adjoint with respect to the reference changes the $r_i$, at a rate we give exactly. For fields, a vacuum is unitarily implementable relative to a reference exactly when it lies at finite distance from it in the space of vacua. For a massless field in de Sitter space we revisit the two canonical charts compared by Grain and Vennin: relative to the reference of the standard squeezing formalism the Bunch--Davies state has $\sinh r_k=1/(2|kη|)$, and relative to the vacuum that a radiation era beginning at time $η$ would select it has $\sinh r_k=1/(2k^2η^2)$. The second comparison squeezes twice as fast and is unitarily implementable; the first is not.

candidates.title: Inflation with an Exponential Power-Law Potential:Analytical Slow-Roll Relations, Branch Dynamics, and Conditional Reheating Matching
candidates.abstract: We study canonical single-field inflation driven by the potential $V(φ)=M^4\exp(φ/M_{\rm Pl})(1+kφ/M_{\rm Pl})^{-1/k}$ with $k<0$. We retain the canonical Einstein--scalar action and derive analytical relations within the slow-roll approximation. Expressing the local spectra through the logarithmic slope $A=kx/(1+kx)$, with $x=φ/M_{\rm Pl}$, yields an endpoint-independent consistency relation among the scalar tilt, tensor ratio, and running at their stated approximation orders. On the negative-field branch, an exact phase-space argument shows that an initially downhill, inflationary hilltop trajectory cannot end inflation within the bare single-field model. We specify the endpoint as a phenomenological input and use a Lambert-$W$ solution of the slow-roll e-fold integral. Tables and figures illustrate the fixed choice $x_e=-2$ and must be interpreted conditionally on a completion that implements this endpoint and preserves the adiabatic spectrum. The reheating-matching relation uses explicit scale and thermal conventions and imposes both endpoint energy bounds and nonnegative reheating duration. The observational comparison uses published marginalized intervals rather than reconstructed joint posteriors. These results establish local analytical structure and conditional numerical benchmarks. A complete exit mechanism, a unique reheating equation of state, and precision spectral predictions remain unestablished.

candidates.title: Probing scalar-mediated Lorentz violation with hydrogen masers and spin-precession of molecules

These experimental approaches provide access to previously unexplored regions of parameter space, probing interaction ranges extending from centimeter to sub-angstrom scales. Our proposals highlight the potential of precision atomic and molecular experiments to search for new spin-dependent scalar-mediated interactions and violations of fundamental spacetime symmetries.

candidates.title: Hidden wormholes from an action principle in $D=4$
candidates.abstract: We present new black hole solutions for the class of gravitational effective field theories in four spacetime dimensions that extend General Relativity while retaining the graviton as the only degree of freedom of gravitational origin. They are regular and have no inner horizon, thus evading the mass inflation instability that afflicts conventional regular black hole geometries.

candidates.title: Spectral recurrences and maximal analyticity: cosmological correlators at one and two loops
candidates.abstract: We develop a method for computing de Sitter boundary correlators based on the maximal analyticity of the two-point function and differential--difference equations satisfied by Schwinger--Keldysh diagrams. The vertex integrations are analytically continued through the relevant de Sitter tuboids onto purely imaginary Lobachevskij cycles. Taking the Mehler--Fock transform of the invariant bubble kernels on these Riemannian cycles converts their differential--difference equations into algebraic recurrences in the spectral parameter. The mixed-branch kernel obeys a homogeneous recurrence, whereas the chronological and antichronological kernels satisfy sourced recurrences whose local terms are determined by dimensionally continued tadpoles. We solve these recurrences, constructing explicit particular solutions in terms of generalised hypergeometric functions and identifying the analytic conditions selecting their physical completion. Attachment to the external boundary points then yields an intrinsic spectral representation and a complete solution of the boundary in--in diagrams considered here. Our method is fully coordinate-independent. Specialising to a Poincaré chart readily gives expressions that can be compared directly with those obtained by the standard coordinate-dependent approach. Composing two or more bubbles yields a multi-loop chain whose spectral multiplier is determined by the one-loop building blocks and the sum over intermediate Schwinger--Keldysh branches.

This result will have far reaching consequences for the study of thermodynamical viability of various gravitational collapse and cosmological solutions of Einstein field equations.

candidates.title: 'Forward-backward' flows and integration cycles for semiclassical Euclidean gravity
candidates.abstract: Integrating Euclidean semiclassical gravity over real Riemannian metrics is subtle due to the conformal factor problem. A perturbative prescription was given by Gibbons-Hawking-Perry (GHP) where the integration contour for the conformal perturbations is rotated to be imaginary. A potential non-perturbative remedy is that the integration cycles associated to semiclassical saddle points should be deformed into the space of complex metrics in the sense of Picard-Lefschetz theory. Here we propose a non-perturbative construction of such complex integration cycles. This employs a 'forward-backward' gradient flow of the Einstein-Hilbert action, starting at a saddle point, along which the action has monotonically increasing real part and constant imaginary part. The flow is not parabolic. In a neighbourhood of a saddle point, the real part of the conformal factor flows forward and that of the conformal class backwards, with the opposite true of their imaginary parts. Starting the flow at a saddle point, then roughly speaking, one specifies the real part of the conformal class and the imaginary part of the conformal factor at the end of the flow. Solving the flow one finds the complex metrics along a one parameter path within the integration cycle of that saddle, and varying this final data generates the integration cycle, the Lefschetz thimble of the saddle point. We find that near to a real saddle point this reproduces the GHP prescription. We characterise the neighbourhood of a saddle where such forward-backward flows may exist, finding a weaker restriction than that of Kontsevich-Segal-Witten. We numerically demonstrate flows explicitly for 4-dimensional gravity, constructing sections through the integration contours for the saddles given by Euclidean de Sitter, and for Schwarzschild in a cavity.

candidates.title: The Stability of the Higgs vacuum inside a Schwarzschild Black Hole
candidates.abstract: I investigate the behaviour of the Higgs field inside a Schwarzschild black hole, including a Planck-suppressed coupling between the Higgs field and the Kretschmann scalar, the leading curvature invariant in a Ricci-flat geometry. Because the radial coordinate is timelike in the interior, the Higgs condensate evolves in time rather than tracking the minimum of its potential. Near the singularity the interior field equation reduces to Bessel's equation, with solution $H=vJ_0(x)$, where $x\propto\sqrtξ\,t_p/τ$ and $τ$ is the proper time to the singularity. Contrary to static analyses, the field remains frozen in its broken phase while the potential changes shape, departing from its vacuum value only when the curvature becomes Planckian, independently of the black-hole mass. Including the one-loop correction from Higgs vacuum fluctuations yields the same Bessel equation with a source term, which I solve exactly; the condensate is reduced by at most about ten per cent. The electroweak symmetry therefore remains broken throughout the interior within the regime of validity of effective field theory.

candidates.title: Probing Velocity-Dependent WIMP Dark Matter Annihilation in Large-Scale Structure
candidates.abstract: The unresolved gamma-ray background (UGRB) provides a promising avenue for probing the cosmological annihilation of weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter through its cross-correlation with large-scale structure (LSS). While most previous studies have assumed a velocity-independent (s-wave) annihilation cross section, many well-motivated particle physics models predict annihilation rates that depend on the relative velocity of dark matter particles. In this work, we develop a generalized halo-model framework to investigate the cosmological signatures of velocity-dependent WIMP annihilation. Parameterizing the velocity-weighted annihilation cross section as $σv_{\rm rel}\propto v_{\rm rel}^{n}$, we consider four representative cases corresponding to Sommerfeld-like (n=-1), s-wave (n=0), p-wave (n=2), and d-wave (n=4) annihilation. We show that velocity dependence modifies not only the overall annihilation emission but also the halo population dominating the signal, leading to distinct effective halo biases, redshift distributions, and angular clustering properties. As a result, different annihilation mechanisms leave characteristic signatures in the UGRB-LSS cross-correlation that cannot be captured by the overall gamma-ray intensity alone. As an illustration of the formalism, we perform a statistical forecast for the cross-correlation between the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) UGRB and the Two Micron All Sky Survey Redshift Survey (2MRS) galaxy catalog and derive the projected sensitivities to the velocity-independent annihilation coefficient for these four annihilation scenarios. Our results demonstrate that cosmological cross-correlations provide a powerful and complementary probe of velocity-dependent dark matter annihilation, offering a new avenue for constraining the particle physics of dark matter through its imprints on large-scale structure.

candidates.title: Active Galactic Nuclei as Beyond the Standard Model Laboratories: a White Paper
candidates.abstract: Multi-messenger and multi-wavelength observations of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) can provide otherwise inaccessible knowledge about physics Beyond the Standard Model (BSM), and may even lead to its discovery. Realizing this potential hinges on two parallel efforts: advancing our understanding of AGN and of the dark matter around them, and identifying the BSM signatures that are at once promising and robust against the gaps in that understanding. These fields have attracted growing interest in recent years, also motivated by the IceCube association of neutrinos to individual AGN, yet we have only begun to explore their cross-fertilization. This white paper offers a new perspective on this interdisciplinary endeavor. It concisely reviews the state of the art in each field and at their interface, and identifies the key open questions that must be addressed to strengthen our prospects for learning about BSM physics with AGN.

candidates.title: QPO constraints on the rotating Fan-Wang spacetime
candidates.abstract: In this work, we investigate a rotating regular black hole described by the Fan-Wang solution, which arises from nonlinear electrodynamics coupled to gravity. We examine the motion of neutral test particles along circular equatorial orbits and derive the corresponding orbital parameters, including the angular velocity, specific angular momentum, and specific energy. By perturbing these orbits in the radial and vertical directions, we calculate the associated fundamental epicyclic frequencies. We then employ the relativistic precession model to interpret the observed quasiperiodic oscillations (QPOs) in terms of these frequencies. We numerically determine the radii of the innermost stable circular orbits and perform Markov chain Monte Carlo simulations to constrain the spacetime parameters. Using observational and theoretical estimates of the black hole mass and spin parameter from the literature, together with theoretically motivated priors on the Fan-Wang parameter, we obtain the best-fit parameter values. The inferred black hole mass, spin parameter, and QPO emission radii are consistent with the corresponding estimates reported in the literature. Furthermore, the dimensionless Fan-Wang parameter satisfies $l/M < 8/27 \approx 0.296$, in agreement with its theoretical upper bound.

candidates.title: Current Accretion State versus Black Hole Mass: Imprints on Multiphase Gas in IllustrisTNG
candidates.abstract: The coupling between AGN feedback and the multiphase circumgalactic medium (CGM) is central to understanding galaxy evolution. In a previous paper, we showed that the black hole mass ($M_{\rm BH}$) correlates negatively with cold gas mass in IllustrisTNG100. We now extend this to the Eddington ratio ($λ_{\rm Edd}$), which traces the current accretion state, using the same sample of 5089 central galaxies at $z=0$ under the same group-specific partial correlation framework, controlling for stellar and dark matter halo mass. We find that $λ_{\rm Edd}$ correlates positively with warm gas in star-forming galaxies ($ρ\approx 0.6$-$0.7$), persisting after jointly controlling for $M_{\rm BH}$, the mass in the other non-star-forming gas phases, and specific star formation rate. The $λ_{\rm Edd}$-cold gas correlation instead reverses sign, from negative in star-forming galaxies ($ρ\approx -0.32$) to positive in quenched galaxies ($ρ\approx 0.40$). Controlling for $M_{\rm BH}$ leaves this correlation essentially unchanged in all three galaxy types. Further controlling for the total gas mass in the other phases strengthens the star-forming correlation and weakens the quenched correlation to $ρ\approx 0.21$, which remains significant. These results establish the Eddington ratio as a phase- and type-dependent tracer of the gas-black hole connection: the cold gas reservoir records the integrated black hole growth, the warm gas in star-forming galaxies carries the signature of the current accretion state, and the sign reversal of the cold-gas correlation marks the transition between the star-forming and quenched regimes.

candidates.title: Worldviews in Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are often described in terms of personas and this framing has become central to alignment research. In this paper, we argue that there is a deeper level of description that lies in the agent's worldviews, i.e., its beliefs about what reality is and how it works. Treating LLMs as a population of subjects, we administer two worldview surveys from human psychology to eight models. We show that the models share many key worldview positions. For example, LLMs consistently describe the world as less good, safe, enticing, and alive than humans do. On the other hand, base models have a more positive outlook, suggesting that the bleakness we found is driven by post-training. In line with research on LLM "personas", we show that system prompts eliciting different identities shift worldviews in consistent directions, and that a contemplative prompt creates a more positive outlook and improves safety. We also found that dialogue between models consistently shifts worldviews and that several models converge on the "spiritual bliss" attractor. Intriguingly, dialogue increased safe responses and the spiritual bliss attractor engendered the most aligned responses overall. These findings suggest that worldviews form a measurable and malleable layer of LLM behavior that may be crucial for robust, positive alignment.

candidates.title: Adaptive LLM-Driven Honeypots vs. LLM-Driven Attackers: Does Narrative Coherence Improve Deception?
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) enable honeypots to generate responses and deceptive artefacts on demand, yet existing approaches evaluate generated content one reply at a time and leave open whether artefacts that jointly describe a coherent event retain an attacker better than unrelated ones. This question becomes pressing as autonomous LLM-driven offensive agents emerge as realistic adversaries. This paper proposes narrative deception, a reactive strategy in which the defender maps each observed attacker command to a MITRE ATT&CK technique, selects a compatible scenario from a curated catalogue based on MITRE Engage, and deploys mutually referential artefacts (files, processes, services, and logs) on an emulated Ubuntu host while the intrusion is under way. An LLM-powered defender and an autonomous LLM attacker interact through a real SSH session, and the attacker's termination policy distinguishes abandonment due to suspected deception from abandonment due to loss of interest. A campaign of 1,150 sessions compares four conditions of increasing sophistication (Static, Same-TTP, Multi-TTP, and Chain) across four open-weight attacker models, four defender models, and three attacker skill levels. Engagement increases significantly at every step. With the same artefact budget per reaction, coherent scenarios raise the median session length of advanced attackers from 40 to 165 commands and reduce their abandonment from 86% to 52%. The effect grows with attacker skill, holds across all sixteen model pairs, and comes at comparable inference cost. Nearly all sessions ended through loss of interest rather than detection, which suggests that deception should sustain meaningful findings, not only emulator fidelity.

candidates.title: The Between-Round Decision in Autonomous Research: An LLM Controller That Reads the Whole Trajectory
candidates.abstract: Executing an idea often changes how promising it looks, so the next step in autonomous research should rest on results, not on proposals. After each round of experiments, the system must decide whether to refine the best solution or start a new direction, which solution to build from, and what goal to set. We call this the between-round decision. Existing systems wrap it in machinery such as rules, scores, search trees, and schedules; where an LLM makes it, what the LLM needs to read is left open. We ask whether an LLM can make this decision from accumulated evidence, without a search structure around it, and how much of that evidence it needs to read. We present BRED (Between-Round Evidence-based Decision), an LLM-based controller that maintains the best verified solution so far (the Champion) and a log of past rounds, and makes one decision per round. On three widely used research-agent benchmark tasks, BRED improves on the task baselines by 4.80% in MAE on ETTh1 (to 0.4172) and by 3.44 and 3.43 points of accuracy on SST-2 (to 95.07%) and CIFAR-100 (to 84.63%), ahead of the published results. When the controller does not read the accumulated evidence, the same loop gains less: with no history it reaches 0.4299 on ETTh1 and 83.71% on CIFAR-100, whereas the full controller's MAE is 2.95% lower and its accuracy 0.92 points higher. On a new task, speech-based depression detection under a leakage-free protocol, it reaches a macro-F1 of 0.6164 on seeds held out from selection, 5.5 points above its baseline and 4.0 above the strongest published system. Code is available at https://github.com/learninginvision/BRED.

candidates.title: DAQ: Decision-Aligned Post-Training Quantization for Spiking Transformers
candidates.abstract: Spiking transformers combine attention-based representation learning with sparse spike communication, yet their weights and membrane variables still incur substantial storage and computation overhead. Post-training quantization (PTQ) offers a practical way to reduce these overheads, but preserving neuronal firing under weight and membrane quantization remains challenging. In this paper, we propose Decision-Aligned Post-Training Quantization (DAQ), a method that calibrates the quantizers to align neuronal firing decisions with those of a floating-point reference. We analyze how errors from these quantizers affect firing at decision boundaries and how they propagate over time steps in recurrent neurons. Based on this analysis, we formulate an objective that encourages quantized membrane variables to remain within the reference firing regions along the quantized model's own state trajectory. Experiments across multiple spiking transformer architectures on image classification, semantic segmentation, and event-based tracking demonstrate the effectiveness of DAQ with 4-bit weights and membrane variables. On FE108, DAQ achieves 58.8\% AUC and 90.9\% PR with SDTrack, while reducing energy by 66.2\%.

candidates.title: Shadows and Images of Black Holes with Purely Nonlinear Scalarization
candidates.abstract: We investigate the shadows and radiative images of static, spherically symmetric black holes with purely nonlinear scalarization in Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet gravity. The quartic exponential coupling supports scalarized backgrounds without a linear tachyonic instability of Schwarzschild black holes. We compare mass and coupling dependences and construct images on radially stable backgrounds using optically thin spherical emission and face-on thin disks. On the sampled radially stable branches, we find smaller shadow radii than those of Schwarzschild black holes at the same mass, with reductions reaching approximately $21.7\%$. The sampled radially unstable branches show much smaller shadow-size deviations. The photon-orbit index, which measures radial instability per unit orbital angle, varies nonmonotonically even when the normalized shadow radius changes monotonically. The index also controls the asymptotic compression of higher-order images, providing information complementary to shadow size. For spherical emission, radial infall produces a darker center relative to the bright ring than static emission. For circular disks, we find that smooth metric variations can create an unstable interval separating two stable regions of timelike circular motion. When the disk occupies the stable region connected to infinity, its inner edge moves outward across this transition, suppressing emission inside the geometric shadow boundary while the normalized shadow radius changes only slightly. Our results show that purely nonlinear scalarization can alter images through both photon propagation and the orbital structure of emitting matter, with the visible features depending on the emission model.

candidates.title: Gravitational Light Deflection via Fractional Calculus and Chebyshev Polynomial Approximation
candidates.abstract: We develop a fractional-calculus-based framework for evaluating gravitational light deflection in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes. By introducing a suitable transformation of the radial coordinate, the deflection integral is recast into an Abel-type integral equation, from which the associated kernel is reconstructed using fractional integration. The leading singular behaviour near the photon sphere is isolated analytically, and the remaining regular part is approximated by a finite Chebyshev polynomial expansion. This combination retains the correct strong-field behaviour while providing an efficient numerical representation of the deflection integral. We demonstrate the accuracy of the method using the Schwarzschild spacetime as a benchmark and compare the resulting deflection angles with the standard strong-deflection approximation and a two-term weak-deflection expansion. We further apply the method to calculate strong-field lensing observables, including the limiting angular position, angular separation, and relative magnification of relativistic images, for the supermassive black holes Sgr A*. The results show that the proposed approach provides an accurate and flexible means of evaluating gravitational deflection angles across a broad range of closest-approach radii. The framework can be extended to other static, spherically symmetric black-hole geometries, including solutions arising in modified theories of gravity.

candidates.title: A Proposal for Quantum Reference Frames in Quantum Field Theory and their Experimental Exploration
candidates.abstract: We construct quantum reference frames (QRFs) in quantum field theory, using localized modes of a scalar field as frames for its shift symmetry. We import tools from relativistic quantum information to explicitly compute entropies and correlation measures of relational observables, investigating their frame dependence and the new features arising from the field-theoretic character of the system. Unlike QRFs for systems with finitely many degrees of freedom, localized field-theoretic QRFs are necessarily mixed in physically relevant states and generically correlated with the subsystems they describe. These aspects of QRFs for fields affect the properties of relational observables in a subtle way. Furthermore, we put forward a proposal for testing these predictions with existing quantum simulators based on ultracold atoms and quantum fluids, thus connecting QRF physics with analogue gravity platforms.

candidates.title: Cyclic Boson Stars with Quantum Vortex Molecules
candidates.abstract: We find a new type of stationary boson star with cyclic rotational symmetry in the minimal model of complex scalar field coupled to gravity. Unlike conventional axisymmetric spinning boson stars, these configurations can carry noninteger angular momentum per particle in units of the reduced Planck constant, revealing a new way for boson stars to carry angular momentum. We identify the vortex assemblies within these stars as self-gravitating quantum vortex molecules, in which gravity supports a stationary vortex arrangement despite internal circulation. These structures provide a relativistic realization of quantum vortex molecules studied in condensates and motivate possible laboratory analogues.

candidates.title: Gravity/Thermodynamics Correspondence for Generic Dynamical Spacetimes
candidates.abstract: Working within covariant phase space formalism, we establish \textit{gravity-thermodynamics correspondence} for generic dynamical spacetimes. We derive local first and second laws of thermodynamics on general null boundaries, for generic non-stationary solutions to Einstein gravity {with minimally coupled matter} for physical observers that we carefully specify. Entropy variation, which receives contribution only from the gravitational sector, is the surface charge variation associated with a vector field generating the null boundary, and temperature is its non-affinity parameter (divided by $2π$). The statement of the second law in our setting is that the entropy variation evaluated along the null vector field is strictly non-negative for the admissible positive-non-affinity clock and matter satisfying the null energy condition. Our dynamical entropy variation, which is non-integrable for generic non-stationary solutions, becomes integrable in near-stationary configurations, reproducing the Hollands--Wald--Zhang dynamical entropy formula. Strikingly, this local second law holds even when the boundary area is decreasing, disentangling thermodynamic irreversibility and the second law from standard area theorems. Our first-principles construction demonstrates that gravitational thermodynamics requires neither a stationary background, teleological event horizons, nor an exact entropy state function on individual codimension-1 spacelike slices of the null boundary (codimension two in spacetime).

candidates.title: A separation criterion for chiral systems and its application to Plebański--Demiański perturbations
candidates.abstract: We give a constructive criterion for local separation of first-order chiral systems coupling two complex doublets. It combines a Gram decomposition of the coupling sources with separate coordinate dependence and a differential transport test. For recoverable, nondegenerate source families, the criterion is necessary and sufficient within the specified class of mode-independent complex matrix transformations with unit determinant. For a fixed differential operator and admissible Gram decomposition, we identify conditions under which the sources uniquely determine the Hermitian coefficient matrix required for separation. As an application, we construct an explicit algebraic transformation and derive separated radial and angular equations for coupled radiative Einstein--Maxwell perturbations of rotating, charged Plebański--Demiański backgrounds with acceleration, NUT charge, and a cosmological constant, on specified local patches. Its Gram decomposition is unique under additional generic assumptions. We also derive angular endpoint indices for Bonnor and Misner identifications with conical deficits or excesses. Under the stated regularity assumptions, each specified self-adjoint angular realization at fixed real mode parameters has a discrete spectrum and a complete orthonormal eigenbasis.

candidates.title: On the Asymptotic Expansion of Massive Fields in Spherically Symmetric Systems
candidates.abstract: The behavior of massive real scalar fields, when sourced by a central object, is usually assumed to follow a Yukawa falloff towards radial infinity. In this paper, we show that this is generically not the case, even for minimally coupled fields. Further, while the point-particle action provides a coordinate-invariant definition of the central object's scalar charge, we show that the coefficient one usually extracts at asymptotically large radii in the case of massive scalar fields is neither coordinate invariant nor identical to the scalar charge appearing in the point-particle action. We resolve this issue perturbatively by constructing matched asymptotic expansions and investigate the non-perturbative structure using numerical methods.

candidates.title: On the toric Bando--Kasue--Nakajima conjecture
candidates.abstract: The conjecture of Bando, Kasue, and Nakajima asserts that every simply connected Ricci-flat $4$-manifold that is asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE), that is, asymptotic at infinity to a flat cone $\mathbb{R}^4/Γ$, is hyperkähler for one of its orientations. A toric ALE instanton is a Ricci-flat ALE $4$-manifold with an effective isometric action of the $2$-torus; such a manifold is simply connected. We prove the conjecture for the toric ALE instantons whose group at infinity $Γ$ is conjugate in $\mathrm O(4)$ to a subgroup of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$: each of them is a multi-Eguchi--Hanson metric with collinear centres. In particular, the conjecture holds for toric ALE instantons with $|Γ|\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}$. The proof uses a closed formula for toric gravitational instantons, which expresses the metric through Hankel determinants of a positive measure on the fixed points of the torus action. With it, the problem becomes a question about lattice points in a parallelogram determined by the end.

candidates.title: Carroll Double Copy
candidates.abstract: We construct a double copy for Carroll gravity as the ``square'' of Carroll Yang-Mills theory at the linearised level. Starting from the convolutional double copy prescription in Lorentzian spacetime, we take the Carrollian limit $c \rightarrow 0$ to establish a double copy dictionary compatible both with symmetries and the corresponding equations of motion. Since this limit yields two distinct sectors, namely the electric and magnetic Carroll theories, we systematically investigate double copy constructions involving all possible combinations of these parent theories. To accommodate the time-independent on-shell configurations of the magnetic Carroll fields, we introduce a suitable regularisation procedure for the convolutional double copy. In addition, the covariance of the double copy under Carroll boosts requires an appropriate dressing of the fields, leading to the inclusion of a Goldstone-type object in the construction. We first develop the formalism using toy models involving scalar fields and then apply it to the double copy between linearised Carroll Yang-Mills theory and Carroll gravity.

candidates.title: Triangle singularity with different dynamical couplings
candidates.abstract: We carry out a systematic study of the impact of dynamical couplings of the vertices on the manifestations of the triangle singularity (TS) in the loop amplitude. Twelve combinations of external and internal spin-parity quantum numbers, covering the $PPS$, $VPP$, $VVP$, $VPA$, $VVV$, $VVA$, and $VVS$ effective vertices, are enumerated. Each loop amplitude is reduced via the Passarino--Veltman decomposition into scalar integrals $A_{0}$, $B_{0}$, and $C_{0}$, whose Lorentz-scalar coefficients encode the dynamical content of the vertices. Using the masses and kinematics of the $η(1405)\toπ^{+}π^{-}π^{0}$ transition via the $K^{*}\bar{K}K$ loop with the intermediate $f_{0}(980)$ resonance in the $π^+π^-$ invariant spectrum as a common numerical benchmark for the twelve spin-parity assignments, we find that the same loop topology produces three distinct phenomena which manifest through the lineshapes, i.e. a narrow peak dominated by the $C_{0}$ contribution; a suppressed peak in which the $B_{0}$ and $C_{0}$ function contributions are comparable; and a cusp-like profile in which the coefficient of the leading Landau logarithm vanishes at the physical TS point. These results indicate that the visibility of a TS enhancement is not fixed by the Landau condition alone but reshaped by the detailed dynamics involved in the loop transitions.

candidates.title: AfriNORM: An Evaluation Benchmark for Normative Reasoning of LLMs Across African Cultures
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed across various sectors. However, current evaluation benchmarks are insufficient to assess the applicability of these models in local African contexts, as most focus on linguistic fluency (grammar/translation) rather than cultural competence. The few existing benchmarks that measure general knowledge or social conventions do not capture the African deontic modality, i.e., the strict norms and taboos that govern diverse social interactions. In this paper, we introduce AfriNORM, a scenario-based, multiple-choice question dataset designed to measure and diagnose the normative reasoning limitations of LLMs when applied to African sociocultural contexts. We introduce two metrics: a Universal Commonsense Bias Score (UCBS) to quantify commonsense bias in LLM and a Distractor Bias Score (DBS) to quantify an LLM's limited understanding of African cultural norms. We also conduct a case study on the Yorùbá language, identifying confusion gaps in two closed-source LLMs, "Gemini 2.0 Flash" and "GPT-5", and one open-source LLM, "Llama 3.1 8B Instruct" when prompted in English versus Yorùbá. While their accuracy in English is high, their performance in Yorùbá is much lower, attributable to cultural confusion rather than simple bias, indicating that the models exhibit semantic confusion when reasoning about norms in Yorùbá.

candidates.title: Do LLMs Understand Network Traces? A Comparative Study of Reasoning over Raw and Filtered Traffic Data
candidates.abstract: The effective delivery and monitoring of ICT services rely heavily on network traffic analysis. However, interpreting complex packet captures remains a challenging task that requires substantial technical expertise. Large language models (LLMs) offer promising opportunities to automate network traffic in- vestigation, yet their reliability in packet-level field extraction and flow-level sequence reconstruction remains an open research question. This study proposes a reproducible, question-answering- based evaluation methodology to assess the capabilities of LLMs in network trace analysis. Using real-world benign traffic from the CICIDS2017 dataset, we evaluate multiple models against a human-generated ground truth, comparing their performance on raw textual traffic dumps and protocol-filtered representations. Model responses are assessed through an automated LLM- as-a-judge pipeline, validated against human evaluations. The results demonstrate that protocol filtering significantly reduces prompt overhead while improving answer accuracy by reducing incorrect responses. These findings highlight the importance of protocol-aware traffic filtering as an effective optimization for improving the efficiency and reliability of LLM-assisted network management.

candidates.title: Flavor Entanglement as a CPT Violation Witness in Neutrino Oscillations
candidates.abstract: We present a comprehensive study linking the single-particle flavor entanglement of a \(ν_{e} \rightarrow ν_μ\) oscillation to CPT violation using the concurrence. In a two-flavor vacuum with CP-conserving mixing, CPT invariance strictly demands \(\mathcal{C}_ν(L) = \mathcal{C}_{\barν}(L)\), meaning any measured difference \(Δ\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{CPT}} \equiv \mathcal{C}_ν - \mathcal{C}_{\barν}\) serves as a clean, background-free witness of CPT violation. We derive exact, first-order analytical relations connecting this entanglement asymmetry to the standard probability asymmetry, the baseline reflection sums, and the long-baseline decoherence floor. To rigorously test the experimental viability of this framework, we perform extensive numerical simulations. We demonstrate that the framework projects stringent sensitivity limits on Standard-Model Extension (SME) parameters at DUNE-like densities, isolate a coordinate-independent CPT invariant, and show that the signal remains robust across realistic, variable Earth matter density profiles. Crucially, we identify a distinct 24-hour sidereal modulation of the entanglement asymmetry, providing a definitive temporal "smoking gun" to disentangle CPT violation from matter effects. Finally, we show that at PeV astrophysical energies, the reflection-sum mismatch scales up to \(10^{13}\) meters, opening a novel frontier for CPT tests beyond terrestrial experiments.

candidates.title: Mapping the multimessenger horizon for $γ$-ray counterparts of cosmic neutrinos
candidates.abstract: The joint detection of high-energy neutrinos and $γ$-rays offers a powerful probe of the most energetic astrophysical accelerators, linking hadronic interactions to observable signatures across cosmic distances. Understanding the conditions under which these two messengers can be simultaneously observed is essential for identifying and characterizing the sources of cosmic neutrinos. In this work, we examine the detectability of $γ$-ray cascades associated with neutrino production in source environments that are gamma-ray transparent, focusing on how electromagnetic cascades evolve as $γ$-rays propagate through intergalactic space. By modeling photon interactions with the extragalactic background light and deflections in intergalactic magnetic fields, we determine the minimum neutrino fluence for transient emission and neutrino flux for steady emission required to produce a $γ$-ray counterpart detectable by $γ$-ray observatories, such as Fermi-LAT, HAWC, or LHAASO. This defines a ``multimessenger horizon" -- the region in flux-distance parameter space where neutrinos and $γ$-rays are jointly observable. We consider both energy-binned injection tied to IceCube's sensitivity and a continuous power-law spectrum extending from TeV to PeV energies. Our results reveal that detectability depends strongly on redshift, magnetic field strength, and photon energy, with higher-energy cascades suffering greater attenuation inside filamentary structures. The framework provides new constraints on source opacity, baryon loading, and neutrino production mechanisms, offering a predictive tool for interpreting current events and guiding future multimessenger campaigns.

candidates.title: Flash UV Spectroscopy: Decoding the Ultraviolet Diversity of Young Core-Collapse Supernovae with the Hubble Space Telescope
candidates.abstract: We present multi-wavelength observations and modeling of the largest sample to date of core-collapse supernovae (SNe) with Hubble Space Telescope (HST) ultraviolet (UV) spectroscopy within < 2 weeks of first light. Our total sample contains early-time UV spectroscopy from 12 Type II SNe (SNe II), 3 Type IIb SNe (SNe IIb), 3 Type IIn SNe (SNe IIn) and 1 Type I super-luminous SN (SLSN-I). This sample includes 11 objects with unpublished UV spectroscopy from HST Cycles 31 and 32 "Flexible Thursdays" target of opportunity programs, increasing the number of core-collapse SNe with early-time HST UV spectra by a factor of 2.4. The early-time near-UV spectra of most sample SNe II show similar Doppler-broadened P-Cygni profiles of metals (Mg, Fe, Ti, Cr), though with notable diversity in line velocities and absorption strengths. Comparison to non-Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (nLTE) radiative transfer model grids at similar phases indicates that most sample SNe II are consistent with low circumstellar material (CSM) densities at the time of UV observations (e.g., $\dot M = 10^{-6}$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$, $v_w = 50$ km/s) and standard kinetic energies (e.g., $E_k = 0.6-1.2$ B), while two objects, SNe 2024faq and 2023ixf, show UV/optical evidence for interaction with more confined, higher-density CSM. SN 2023ixf and sample SNe IIn exhibit relatively featureless early-time UV spectra despite displaying prominent optical Lorentzian emission lines from electron scattering in optically thick CSM -- this being attributed to differing properties of UV resonance versus optical recombination transitions as well as intrinsic CSM asymmetries. These results demonstrate the potential of early-time UV spectroscopy to constrain the outermost SN ejecta structure, explosion energetics/composition, and progenitor mass-loss histories of core-collapse SNe.

candidates.title: Cross-cultural Adaptation of Recipes for Low-Resource Languages: A Benchmark and Multilingual Culinary Lexicon for Hausa, Yorùbá, and Igbo
candidates.abstract: Recent multilingual large language models (LLMs) have improved machine translation, yet culturally adaptive translation for low-resource languages (LRLs) remains underexplored. This is particularly challenging for recipes, where ingredients, cooking tools, measurements, and procedures may require adaptation to the target cultural context. In this work, we introduce ReciLoReL, a benchmark of 600 expert-translated and culturally adapted recipes across Yorùbá, Hausa, and Igbo (three of the most prominent languages in Nigeria), and ReciLex, a multilingual culinary lexicon containing approximately 15,000 translated entities across ten recipe entity categories, including ingredients, tools, chef actions, state of tools, and durations. We evaluate state-of-the-art multilingual LLMs for English-to-LRL recipe translation under zero-shot and few-shot settings and investigate whether augmenting LLMs with ReciLex improves culturally adaptive recipe translation without requiring large target-language recipe corpora for training or fine-tuning. Beyond conventional reference-based translation evaluation using BLEU, chrF, and TER, we introduce five criteria for evaluating cultural adaptation, adapted from established cross-cultural adaptation methods. Across the selected LLMs and languages, ReciLex improves average BLEU from 13.57 to 14.51 and chrF from 37.89 to 38.74, while reducing TER from 77.14 to 75.12. Human evaluation further shows improvements ranging from 0.11 to 0.36 points across the five cultural adaptation evaluation criteria on a five-point scale. Overall, our work provides new resources, evaluation criteria, and empirical evaluation for studying culturally adaptive recipe translation in low-resource settings.

candidates.title: Contract-Explicit Evaluation: From Auditing Learned Readers to Scoped Certificates
candidates.abstract: Evaluation readings of document-level relation extraction (DocRE) systems depend jointly on the model and the evaluation contract: gold version, scoring function, threshold. Rankings reverse across contracts, yet no existing method determines which comparisons survive the reversal. We address this gap with contract-explicit evaluation: a preregistered five-step protocol (Declare, Measure, Scope, Certify, Hedge), operationalizing the classical concordance decomposition of Kendall's rank correlation, that scopes certifiable regions and delivers distribution-free census certificates across two ecosystems. In the DocRE audit (44 training runs of one in-house architecture family), the scoring dimension scopes to a census certificate (three flagged instances, Clopper--Pearson upper bound 0.146); the confirmatory record includes registered negatives, and the audit prices its own simplification finding---the calibration dial's entire margin is one withdrawn commit. In an LLM-judge census (17 judges, 49,938 battles), 12.25% of leaderboard comparisons require hedging at the pre-declared split criterion (bound 0.124; panel-robust 0.143), with an exploratory two-tier reading certifying 69% at a bound \le 0.072 and a validity decomposition against released human labels (65% of contested battles are judge error, not ambiguity). The cross-model certificate is withdrawn on real confidence scores; the failure spectrum maps the boundary. The protocol, map, ledger, and per-instance artifacts are released.

candidates.title: Right Diagnosis, Unsafe Route: Auditing Clinical AI Decision Trajectories and Corrective Oversight for Validity and Potential Harm
candidates.abstract: A clinical AI system can reach a correct final diagnosis through intermediate decisions that could have harmed the patient, and can repair an error while introducing new risks. Most evaluations score final diagnoses; even stepwise benchmarks, which release a case's evidence over time, score whether systems reach the right diagnosis or gather the right information, not whether the decisions a patient passes through are safe. We make patient safety the target of stepwise evaluation. A trajectory audit replays real admissions checkpoint by checkpoint, lets each system decide with only the evidence released so far, and rates every test, treatment and disposition for its potential harm to the patient and, separately, for clinical validity, against the documented final diagnosis and physician-written disease rubrics yet on the evidence available when the decision was made. An LLM judge scores every decision, and a physician reference standard (triple annotation and senior adjudication of a stratified sample) calibrates the rates. An oversight audit branches each trajectory at its first actionable error and measures, on the same branches, whether corrective feedback repairs the error and whether it introduces new harm. Across 300 cases from a hospital cardiology cohort, MIMIC-IV and the public ASCENT benchmark, with up to seven AI systems per source, 55.2% of hospital trajectories reaching an acceptable final diagnosis passed through a decision with moderate or severe potential harm and 24.8% through a clinically unacceptable one; the harm rates were 76.2% on MIMIC-IV and 39.6% on ASCENT. Structured corrections resolved 73.6% of first errors versus 24.8% after bare rejection, yet new potentially unsafe decisions followed 30.2% of corrections versus 19.7% of rejections. A correct final diagnosis does not certify a safe trajectory, and a successful correction does not certify a safe recovery.

candidates.title: Neutron-Rich Disks, Nickel-Rich Ejecta: Can Direct-Horizon Collapsars Explain Early $r$-Process Enrichment?
candidates.abstract: Very massive stars above the pair-instability mass gap may collapse directly into black holes surrounded by massive disks. These "direct-horizon collapsars" accrete at $\dot{M} \gtrsim 10\,M_\odot\,{\rm s}^{-1}$ and have been proposed to eject a substantial amount of $r$-process material, powering "super-kilonovae". We present the first three-dimensional general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations of direct-horizon collapsars with M1 neutrino transport, following a $\approx 150\,M_\odot$ helium core from collapse through the escape of magnetically driven outflows. Extreme accretion rates neutronize the disks to $Y_{\rm e} \approx 0.1$-$0.25$ and, at early times, allow them to satisfy the gravitational-instability and cooling criteria for fragmentation. However, the strong poloidal fields needed to eject the neutron-rich gas promptly also drain the disks and lift their electron degeneracy. The neutron-rich ejecta composition is set in a brief phase, such that the ejecta carry $\sim 0.1$-$0.3\,M_\odot$ of nuclei with $A \geq 69$, including $\lesssim 2\times10^{-4}\,M_\odot$ of lanthanides, alongside $\sim 1$-$4\,M_\odot$ of $^{56}$Ni. Assuming proportional retention and mixing of Eu and Fe, these yields imply $[{\rm Eu/Fe}]\approx-0.4$ to $+0.3$, and simple dilution estimates permit enrichment at $[{\rm Fe/H}]\lesssim-2.6$. Direct-horizon collapsars are therefore potential prompt contributors to iron and $r$-process enrichment at low metallicity. Their predicted Eu/Fe ratios fall below those of strongly $r$-process-enhanced stars, but uncertainties in the relative yields, particularly of iron, may close this gap. The ${}^{56}{\rm Ni}$-rich ejecta would power luminous supernovae with rise times of weeks, potentially accompanied by exceptionally powerful gamma-ray bursts, rather than lanthanide-rich super-kilonovae.

candidates.title: Double parton scattering singularities in two-loop gluon-fusion amplitudes
candidates.abstract: Gluon fusion to two massive colour singlets can develop a double parton scattering (DPS) singularity as $p_T\to0$: each gluon splits, and its daughters fuse pairwise. We determine two-loop logarithms using a common kernel and derive finite matching functions analytically for gluon and quark splittings. Normalised to one loop, the cubic coefficient changes sign between channels. Complete $gg\to HH$, $gg\to AA$ and $gg\to ZZ$ amplitudes confirm the predicted colour, helicity and parity dependence and phase. The kernel gives leading DPS logarithms for other pairs with this DPS configuration.

candidates.title: Giant gravitons without giant gravitons
candidates.abstract: We demonstrate that the partition function of a free bosonic $U(N)$ multi-matrix model admits a giant graviton expansion. For $d$ matrices, there are $d$ distinct giant gravitons, and the expansion can be characterized by a $d$-node quiver with bifundamentals connecting the nodes. This suggests the intriguing possibility of a more generalized holography where models without any obvious gravitational dual can nevertheless be given a dual brane interpretation. The giant graviton expansion of this multi-matrix model is somewhat unconventional though, as the giant graviton partition functions will necessarily have intrinsic $N$-dependence.

candidates.title: Center anomalies without twists: torsion, exact degeneracies, and condensates
candidates.abstract: Mixed center anomalies are usually exposed by 't Hooft's twisted boundary conditions in a Hamiltonian formalism. On $\mathbb {RP}^3$, torsion makes the twist unnecessary: a center operator on the untwisted $SU(2)$ Hilbert space anticommutes with time reversal in Yang-Mills theory at $θ=π$ and with the chiral symmetry of super Yang-Mills theory, so every level is at least doubly degenerate. The relevant semiclassical object is the BPST instanton, which descends to a charge-$\tfrac12$ saddle on the orbifold $\mathbb R^4/\mathbb Z_2$. We complete it in two ways: applying a conformal transformation maps the orbifold to $\mathbb R\times\mathbb {RP}^3$, with the saddle describing the tunneling event between the two center sectors; by resolving the orbifold singularity, we obtain the Eguchi-Hanson space, which gives the gaugino condensate at its weak-coupling value.

candidates.title: Low-frequency Radio Observation of the Dark PeVatron LHAASO J2108+5157 Using uGMRT. II
candidates.abstract: We present deep radio observations of the PeVatron candidate LHAASO J2108+5157 using the upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (uGMRT). Our observations reveal a persistent double-lobed radio source (\gmrtext) within the vicinity of the $\geq$100 TeV $γ$-ray emission region, with consistent morphology across 400 MHz, 650 MHz, and 1.2 GHz. No alternative particle accelerators, such as supernova remnants or pulsar wind nebulae, are identified in the region, making \gmrtext\ the most plausible counterpart candidate. We measure the flux and spatially resolved spectra of the source using multi-band radio data. The morphology remains stable across all bands, while a comparison of non-contemporaneous observations suggests possible flux variability. candidates.title: Properties of Chromium and Manganese in Tycho's SNR with XRISM/Resolve
candidates.abstract: The X-ray emission of young supernova remnants gives access to the composition and spatial distribution of elements ejected in supernovae. The emission from the ejecta provides crucial insights into the explosion mechanism, especially for Fe-group elements formed in the innermost layers of the star. The objective of this paper is to provide constraints on the supernova progenitor and explosion mechanism of Tycho's type Ia supernova remnant by studying the properties of Cr and Mn. The unprecedented spectral resolution of XRISM/Resolve allows us to detect significant emission lines of Cr and Mn in different regions of Tycho's supernova remnant, even at small scale, providing a much more precise spatial distribution of Cr and Mn with respect to previous measurements. Significant Cr and Mn emission lines are observed in the Fe bright northeastern-to-southeastern emitting rim, some in the center region, but none in the southern region. The observed mass ratios of Mn/Fe, Cr/Fe and Mn/Cr, are consistent with 1D delayed detonation models of near-Chandrasekhar-mass Type Ia supernovae and 1D pure-detonation models of 1 Msol sub-Chandrasekhar-mass progenitors. In both cases, the observations imply supersolar zero-age main-sequence progenitor metallicities. Overall the best agreement is found for models with a too high metallicity to be realistic for Tycho's location. This points to additional sources of neutronisation such as carbon simmering for Chandrasekhar mass progenitor. For sub-Chandrasekhar mass, double detonation models with a WD mass lower than 1Msol are suggested.
